summary: The migration first sets referrer_id to NULL for any rows where the value does not reference an existing account_user.id, ensuring all remaining non-NULL values satisfy the upcoming FK constraint. Then a foreign key constraint is added referencing account_user(id), allowing both the old and new versions to safely treat referrer_id as a self-reference integer during the overlap. The new version is deployed with state_only migration, and the old version is retired after verification.
write_consistency: referrer_id remains an integer column readable and writable by both old and new versions. The FK constraint enforces that every non-NULL referrer_id references an existing account_user.id, so the new version sees valid references and the old version's writes are accepted as long as they point to valid users. No column type change prevents schema incompatibility during the concurrent period.

stages.description: Set referrer_id to NULL for rows where the value does not reference an existing account_user.id, ensuring all non-NULL values satisfy the upcoming FK constraint.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET referrer_id = NULL WHERE referrer_id IS NOT NULL AND referrer_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM account_user);

stages.description: Add foreign key constraint on account_user.referrer_id referencing account_user(id).
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD CONSTRAINT fk_account_user_referrer FOREIGN KEY (referrer_id) REFERENCES account_user(id);

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version after the new version has been verified running.
